body.cap: RUAHLAB received the CES 2024 Innovation Award with the wearable respiratory measurement and analysis system ‘RUAH.’ │ Photo by AVING News

body.x: RUAHLAB (CEO Lee Tae-yang) participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tue) to 12th (Fri, local time).

RUAHLAB is a technology startup with a core value of promoting human health through research and development related to respiration. In line with this philosophy, the company is researching the RUAH system, which allows individuals to monitor their breathing easily through an app at home. RUAHLAB provides lifestyle health management devices and app services related to breathing, sleep, exercise, and mental health. The company is collaborating with outstanding professors from Hanyang University’s College of Engineering and College of Medicine, conducting R&D and verifying the functionality of RUAH products.

RUAH is a wearable respiratory measurement and analysis system targeting the global sleep apnea diagnosis market. By acquiring and analyzing respiratory-related indicators during sleep, the solution can actively manage abnormal respiration, such as sleep apnea and snoring, that impairs sleep quality. As a result, it has secured clear differentiation from other healthcare solutions. According to the company’s explanation, it simultaneously allows the management of daily health indicators such as sleep, exercise, and mental health.

The RUAH solution, consisting of a dedicated wearable device and app, maximizes the reliability and utility of the data obtained through an AI (artificial intelligence) sleep analysis algorithm. This simple configuration is considered a significant advantage, resolving issues such as the one-time nature and low convenience of the standard sleep apnea test, known as polysomnography.

A representative of RUAHLAB said, “The RUAHLAB team has improved the technological capabilities and accuracy of ‘RUAH’ through various prototype versions. In this process, we also increased our expertise in respiration and sleep by consulting experts and professors from the College of Medicine and Engineering. Efforts were made to solve problems arising from numerous variables. Through these efforts, we also developed an AI sleep analysis algorithm.” He added, “We requested an evaluation from a national certification agency for RUAH and obtained achievements in the minimum flow rate measurement and respiratory rate accuracy sections. In this way, RUAH takes a step closer to the goal of digitalized respiratory management for health management, receiving recognition for its innovation and technological capabilities by winning the CES 2024 Innovation Award.”

body.cap: Lee Tae-yang, CEO of RUAHLAB, demonstrated the ‘RUAH’ solution in person. │ Photo by AVING News

body.x: He continued, “This CES 2024 marks the first success as a global target, and we are preparing for the official launch of the RUA solution in the U.S. market, beyond the domestic market” and said, “The response from visiting companies and consumers during the CES exhibition period was positive. We held meetings with various companies for business purposes, including those that can distribute our products, those with whom we can discuss investment, and those that can help us explore overseas markets. Positive consultations are ongoing. In addition, it was a great opportunity to meet with doctors and medical experts.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
